A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLSA work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C. The reordered material in v2 can be matched reliably to v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original FFHQ and ImageNet generation experiments, attention-efficiency measurements, ablations, training curves, and generated samples in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports the same original generation experiments, efficiency measurements, ablations, training curves, and qualitative samples, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: The hierarchical compression and Top-K selection, KV enrichment and reweighting, sparse-index transpose algorithm, and pixel-DiT adaptations remain unchanged in Algorithms 1-2 and Sections 4-5.1.

E1.justification: Both retain FFHQ training and evaluation across resolutions from 32 to 512, plus ImageNet-128/256 training and evaluation with PixelFlow. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: full attention, VSA, and SLA in Table 2; VSA and SLA in Table 3; and the same baselines in ablations, kernel comparisons, and qualitative results.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and Appendix A retain the same model configurations, training budgets, sampling procedures, matched-K comparisons, and H200 timing settings. Table 4 is unchanged, as are the 10,000-sample evaluations and the pixel-DiT evaluation's 20 diffusion steps.

E4.justification: The attention-design, block-size, Top-K, enrichment-level, 512-resolution scaling, SNR, index-reordering, and pretraining analyses are retained. Tables 1 and 5 and Figures 4-8 contain the same analyses and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The point-estimate and curve reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported results match, including appendix tables, curves, and generated samples. For example, Table 2 retains LLSA FIDs of 24.37 and 39.29, while Table 3 retains FID 20.41, Inception Score 73.21, and throughput 34.16.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, and complexity derivations in Sections 3-4.2 are unchanged. The noise-scheduling equation and appendix SNR formulas also match after accounting for typesetting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about log-linear attention, hierarchical context preservation, and efficient training. The headline 28.27-fold attention-inference and 6.09-fold DiT-training acceleration claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of global-context preservation, quality-efficiency tradeoffs, and kernel scaling are unchanged. Appendix C retains the qualification that FFHQ-512 samples follow only two training epochs and might improve with longer training.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Table 4 preserve the same kernel-implementation clarifications, hyperparameters, pretraining configurations, batch sizes, learning rates, and GPU information. No implementation or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 43 references and the same research positioning in Section 2 are retained. Bibliography relocation and updated citation back-reference page numbers do not change the cited works or their interpretation.

P1.justification: v2 adds a funding acknowledgment and moves the references before Appendices A-C. The main narrative and appendix prose otherwise remain unchanged apart from reflow and the updated arXiv version/date stamp.

P2.justification: Appendix body text decreases from approximately 10-point to 9-point, and reflow relocates Tables 4-5 and Figures 5-8. The figures, table structures, captions, and visual content are retained; the changes concern typography and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution and arranges the references and appendices more compactly, with smaller appendix text as a minor readability tradeoff. The scientific argument, supporting evidence, and reproducibility information are unchanged, so these limited editorial changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
